stories.title: 13th Floor Sells Florida Housing Community for $29M
stories.excerpt: 13th Floor Investments has sold a new housing community designated for residents 55 years and older in West Delray Beach, Fla., for $29.3 million, property records show. Robbins Property Associates purchased the 7.6-acre asset called Solera at Avalon Trails. The community features 74 single-story houses at 14800 Cumberland Drive, about a mile west of the South Jog Road. “Our vision was to deliver a thoughtfully designed community that responded to the evolving needs of active adults who value the flexibility of renting, maintenance-free lifestyle and access to a full suite of amenities,” Mike Nunziata, president 13th Floor Investments’s 13th Floor Homes division, said in a statement. Walker & Dunlop’s Still Hunter represented the Miami-based developer, which completed the development in 2024, a year after securing a $14.1 million construction loan from CIBC Bank. The two- and three-bedroom villas range in size from about 1,300 to 1,450 square feet. Berkadia originated a $19.2 million, fixed-rate acquisition loan for Robbins Property Associates. The brokerage’s Mitch Sinberg, Brad Williamson, Scott Wadler and Hugo Hernandez arranged the 10-year, Freddie Mac-backed loan. The Tampa-based buyer owns two multifamily properties in South Florida. The region has seen an uptick in senior housing sales in recent months. In August, PGIM Real Estate offloaded a relatively new assisted living facility, also in Delray Beach, for at least $140 million. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: 13th Floor Homes sold Solera at Avalon Trails, West Delray Beach, for $29.3M
74-unit age-55+ rental community; Robbins Property Associates financed with $19.2M fixed-rate loan
Strong market signal: newly completed 2024 asset sold quickly with 37% LTC (loan-to-cost)
stories.summary: 13th Floor Investments sold its 74-unit age-55+ rental community Solera at Avalon Trails in West Delray Beach, Florida, to Robbins Property Associates for $29.3 million. The property was completed in 2024 and financed with a $19.2 million acquisition loan from Berkadia. The two- and three-bedroom villas range from 1,300 to 1,450 square feet and offer maintenance-free living and full amenities.
stories.impact: South Florida's 55+ rental segment remains capital-competitive and attractive to institutional buyers, even post-delivery. Strong pricing and fixed-rate financing availability signal continued investor appetite for age-restricted multifamily in high-growth coastal Florida submarkets, supporting continued supply of this demographic-driven asset class.

stories.title: ESRT Faces New Activist Investor Following Stake Acquisition
stories.excerpt: An activist shareholder has arrived at Empire State Building Trust (ESRT). Erez Asset Management, a New Rochelle, N.Y.-based activist investment firm and hedge fund manager, has disclosed its acquisition of 10 million shares, or a 5.8 percent stake, in ESRT, Bisnow first reported. Erez has already begun putting pressure on ESRT leadership to sell some or all of its 8 million-square-foot Manhattan portfolio, Crain’s New York reported, which includes the Empire State Building, 1400 Broadway and 1 Grand Central Place. The acquisition by Erez is likely unwelcome news for Tony Malkin, ESRT’s CEO and controlling shareholder. Shares in the New York-based real estate investment trust (REIT), currently one of New York’s largest landlords, have lost nearly 60 percent of their value over the past two years. They currently trade at around $4.40 per share. Erez plans to have discussions with ESRT’s management and board members about governance, corporate structure, compensations and financial decisions, according to its Securities Exchange Commission (SEC) filing. Erez is managed by Bruce Schanzer, the former CEO of Cedar Realty Trust. Undervalued, small-capitalization real estate stocks are the firm’s speciality. Erez said in its filing that it believes ESRT’s portfolio is undervalued — a common refrain in the world of REITs, although many others have enjoyed some recovery of values this year. ESRT, on the other hand, has seen its market capitalization decline from $3.3 billion in 2024 to just $1.3 billion in recent months. Multiple quarters of earnings calls by ESRT leadership dwelled on declining visits to the Empire State Building’s observatory, largely linked to persistent drops in international tourism. The iconic destination is also contending with new competition from viewing platforms at One Vanderbilt and at Hudson Yards towers. The observatory generated $12.4 million of net operating income in the second quarter of this year, a sharp 48.5 percent decrease from $24.1 m
bullets: Erez Asset Management acquired 5.8% stake (10M shares) in Empire State Realty Trust (ESRT)
Activist pushing sale of 8M-sf Manhattan portfolio; ESRT shares down 60% in two years to $4.40
Leadership pressure on trophy-asset REIT signals office cap-rate compression risk, tenant weakness
stories.summary: Activist hedge fund Erez Asset Management disclosed a 5.8 percent stake in Empire State Realty Trust and is pressuring management to sell some or all of ESRT's 8 million-square-foot Manhattan portfolio, including the Empire State Building, 1400 Broadway, and 1 Grand Central Place. ESRT shares have lost nearly 60 percent of their value over two years and currently trade at $4.40. The activist is engaging with ESRT's board and management.
stories.impact: Significant office distress in Manhattan's CBD despite trophy assets. Activist pressure on a blue-chip REIT signals deepening uncertainty in Manhattan office fundamentals and cap rates; multifamily developers should monitor potential asset sales and market disruption, particularly if conversion opportunities arise in Midtown.

stories.title: Citigroup Supplies $28M Refi for Revived Office Building in Arlington, Va.
stories.excerpt: A Washington, D.C., developer has secured fresh capital to continue engineering the turnaround of a once-struggling office building just across the Potomac River. Jemal Equities, which is run by Douglas Development Managing Principal Matthew Jemal, has landed a $28 million commercial mortgage-backed securities loan to refinance its 10-story office property at 1530 Wilson Boulevard, in Arlington, Va., Commercial Observer has learned. Citigroup provided the loan for the roughly 174,000-square-foot building in Arlington’s Rosslyn neighborhood that Jemal Equities acquired in October 2025 for $28 million from Velocis when it was 61 percent leased. The 1990-built property is now 89 percent leased with a 6.8-year weighted average lease term (WALT) compared to a 2.8 WALT at the time of purchase, according to Meridian Capital Group, which arranged the loan. Meridian’s Cary Pollack and Judah Neuman negotiated the debt. “Matthew Jemal has built a reputation for turning buildings around, and 1530 Wilson is the latest example,” Pollack said in a statement. “What Jemal Equities accomplished here in under a year comes down to grit, hard work and determination. Citi recognized the strength of that execution, and we were able to secure financing that reflects where this building is today and where it’s headed.” The $28 million acquisition by Jemal marked a 61 percent drop from the $71.4 million Velocis paid for the building in April 2020. Recent upgrades include a renovated lobby, an outdoor terrace and a fitness center with locker rooms. A 50-person conference center is under development. Anchor tenants at 1530 Wilson include Lincoln Property Company, Blue Origin and SAS Institute. Citigroup and Jemal Equities did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com
bullets: Jemal Equities refinanced 1530 Wilson Boulevard, Arlington, Va., with $28M CMBS loan from Citi
Office leasing jumped from 61% to 89% in months; WALT extended to 6.8 years post-acquisition
Rosslyn submarket showing strong flight-to-quality recovery; office repositioning working
stories.summary: Jemal Equities secured a $28 million CMBS refinance from Citigroup for 1530 Wilson Boulevard in Arlington's Rosslyn neighborhood. The 174,000-square-foot office building was acquired in October 2025 at 61 percent occupancy and $28 million; it now stands at 89 percent leased with a 6.8-year weighted average lease term. The 1990-built property is attracting quality tenants and demonstrating successful repositioning.
stories.impact: Arlington/Rosslyn office market showing selective strength and flight-to-quality dynamics. Successful repositioning and refinancing at stabilized occupancy signals that well-located, operationally improved office assets remain financeable—relevant for multifamily developers evaluating office-to-residential conversion feasibility in the Washington, D.C. submarket.

stories.title: Three Fashion Tenants Ink Deals at 231 West 39th Street
stories.excerpt: Three women’s apparel brands have taken office and showroom space at 231 West 39th Street in Manhattan’s Garment District, landlord broker and building manager Adams & Company announced Wednesday. Rino & Pelle, a Netherlands-based women’s fashion and accessories brand, has inked a 3,332-square-foot lease at the 12-story building, while luxury women’s wear and fine jewelry brand Valentina Kova took 1,594 square feet, and ready-to-wear resort attire retailer Sister NY scooped up 900 square feet at the property. The length of each lease and the asking rents were not disclosed. The average asking rent for office space in Midtown was $85.08 per square foot during the third quarter of 2026, according to Colliers data. The average asking rent for retail space in nearby Herald Square was $403 per square foot in the third quarter, according to CBRE data. Jeff Buslik from Adams & Company represented the landlord, 231/249 West 39 Street Associates, in all three deals. The tenant brokers were not immediately disclosed. “231 West 39th Street has long served as a destination for apparel brands, designers and manufacturers, and this growing roster of fashion tenants reflects the continued demand for well-located office and showroom space in Manhattan’s Garment District,” Buslik said in a statement. “With more than 85 fashion showrooms in the building, we continue to see companies looking for space that supports both their creative and business operations, while offering the accessibility and amenities of a central Midtown location,” Buslik added. Constructed in 1901, 231 West 39th Street is between Seventh and Eighth avenues. Other tenants in the building include apparel, accessory design and manufacturing company Decor Global, as well as apparel firm Akoo Clothing. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Three women's fashion brands leased 5,826 sf combined at 231 West 39th, Manhattan Garment District
Rino & Pelle (3,332 sf), Valentina Kova (1,594 sf), Sister NY (900 sf); rents not disclosed
Herald Square retail at $403/sf; Midtown office at $85.08/sf—Garment District remains fashion anchor
stories.summary: Three women's apparel brands—Rino & Pelle, Valentina Kova, and Sister NY—leased a combined 5,826 square feet of office and showroom space at 231 West 39th Street in Manhattan's Garment District. Specific lease terms and rates were not disclosed, though market comparables show Herald Square retail at $403 per square foot and Midtown office at $85.08 per square foot. The property continues to serve as a hub for fashion tenants.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact. Fashion district leasing reflects local specialty tenant activity, not broad market demand signals. Relevant to multifamily only if future Garment District office-to-residential conversions are considered; current lease activity suggests continued office utility in this niche.

stories.title: Financial Services Firm Rothera Signs Lease at 242 West 38th Street
stories.excerpt: Cohen Capital and Solomon Acquisitions have signed three new office deals totaling 10,266 square feet at their Garment District office property at 242 West 38th Street, Commercial Observer has learned. The largest of the three deals was signed by Rothera, a derivatives exchange and clearinghouse that took 3,915 square feet on the property’s eighth floor. The length of the lease was not disclosed, but the asking rent was $45 per square foot, according to a source close to the deals. The landlord was represented in all three deals by Newmark’s JD Cohen and Ariel Harwood. Newmark declined to comment on the deals. JD Cohen is also the founder of Cohen Capital. Rothera was represented by David Katz from CBRE, who did not immediately respond to CO’s request for comment. Rothera will relocate from a coworking space, though it is unclear where the temporary office space is located and when Rothera will make the move. Also relocating to 242 West 38th Street is Bader Media. The end-to-end media production firm has signed a 3,651-square-foot lease to occupy space on the building’s 10th floor. The length of the lease was not disclosed, but the asking rent was $43 per square foot, according to the source. Bader Media will eventually relocate from 226 West 26th Street. The tenant was represented by Kyle Berlinsky at Colliers, who did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Meanwhile, SDGi Architects has also found a new home at 242 West 38th Street, having signed a 2,700-square-foot lease to occupy space on the property’s 15th floor with an asking rent of $49 per square foot. The designer will eventually relocate from 200 West 41st Street. Newmark’s Cohen and Hardwood also repped the tenant in this deal. Cohen Capital and Solomon Acquisitions acquired the 14-story office property on West 38th Street for $9 million earlier this year, according to property records. Music instructing company New York Vocal Coaching and 21 Pilates New York are also tenants at the property.
bullets: Rothera (derivatives exchange) leased 3,915 sf at 242 West 38th, Garment District, at $45/sf
Bader Media leased 3,651 sf on 10th floor; both relocating from temporary/coworking space
Garment District office sub $50/sf; flight from coworking signals stabilizing demand
stories.summary: Rothera, a derivatives exchange and clearinghouse, leased 3,915 square feet on the eighth floor of 242 West 38th Street in Manhattan's Garment District at $45 per square foot asking rent. Bader Media, an end-to-end media production firm, also leased 3,651 square feet on the 10th floor. Both tenants are relocating from temporary coworking space. Lease lengths were not disclosed.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact. Garment District micro-leasing to niche tenants relocating from coworking reflects low pricing and flight-to-permanent-space behavior, not broad office recovery. Not a demand signal for residential development.

stories.title: Tribe Buys Scottsdale Princess
stories.excerpt: The San Manuel Investment Authority (SMIA) acquired the Fairmont Scottsdale Princess in Scottsdale, Arizona. Set on 65 acres in the Sonoran Desert, the resort features 750 guest rooms and suites, including the exclusive Privado Villas; the 44,000-square-foot full-service Well & Being Spa; six pools; five food and beverage outlets, including signature restaurants from renowned chefs Richard Sandoval and Michael Mina; and eight retail stores. The resort is adjacent to TPC Scottdale, home of the PGA Tour’s WM Phoenix Open. Additionally, the Princess hosts numerous special events that are popular with locals and visitors alike, including the summer’s Freedom Fest and the beloved Christmas at the Princess holiday festival. The San Manuel Nation is a federally recognized Native American tribe located on the San Manuel Indian Reservation near Highland, California. Last year, the tribe acquired full ownership of Waldorf Astoria Monarch Beach Resort & Club in Dana Point, California. The tribe owns a handful of other high-end resorts. The post Tribe Buys Scottsdale Princess appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: San Manuel Investment Authority acquired Fairmont Scottsdale Princess, 65-acre resort, Scottsdale, Ariz.
750-room resort with spa, pools, restaurants, retail; adjacent to PGA Tour venue TPC Scottdale
Tribal nation expanding hospitality portfolio (prior: Waldorf Astoria Monarch Beach, Dana Point)
stories.summary: The San Manuel Investment Authority, a federally recognized Native American tribe, acquired the Fairmont Scottsdale Princess, a 750-room resort set on 65 acres in Scottsdale, Arizona. The property includes a 44,000-square-foot spa, six pools, five dining outlets, and eight retail stores. The acquisition follows the tribe's 2024 purchase of Waldorf Astoria Monarch Beach Resort & Club in Dana Point, California.
stories.impact: No direct multifamily impact. Hospitality acquisition in resort market; not a signal for apartment demand, supply, or development economics in Scottsdale metro.

stories.title: Dwight Capital Finances $60M Loan for Iowa Multifamily Community
stories.excerpt: Dwight Capital has closed a $60 million HUD 223(f) refinance for Birchwood Grove, a newly developed 194-unit townhome community in Davenport, Iowa. Birchwood Grove is comprised of 56 two- and three-story townhouse buildings, along with a separate community building that houses a clubhouse, leasing office, and 4,800 square feet of ground-floor commercial space. Located at 5101 Ravenwood Lane, the property is in close proximity to walkable amenities, shopping, restaurants and offers easy access to Interstate 74 and 80. Loan proceeds will retire existing debt, cover closing costs, fund a replacement reserve for future capital improvements, and allow the borrower to draw on equity accumulated since the original construction financing. The transaction was originated by Josh Hoffman and Jonathan Pomper on behalf of the borrower, Kevin Dolan, of Dolan Homes LLC. The post Dwight Capital Finances $60M Loan for Iowa Multifamily Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Dwight Capital closed $60M HUD 223(f) refi for Birchwood Grove, Davenport, Iowa, 194 units
Newly developed 56 townhouse buildings plus 4,800-sf ground-floor commercial; close to I-74/80
Strong refinance execution signals Davenport multifamily stabilization and lender confidence
stories.summary: Dwight Capital closed a $60 million HUD 223(f) refinance for Birchwood Grove, a newly developed 194-unit townhome community in Davenport, Iowa. The property consists of 56 two- and three-story townhouse buildings plus a community building with 4,800 square feet of ground-floor commercial space. Loan proceeds retire existing debt, fund reserves, and release accumulated equity to the borrower.
stories.impact: Davenport/Eastern Iowa market shows solid multifamily fundamentals with new supply able to refinance quickly post-delivery at scale. HUD program utilization and strong loan execution signal investor confidence in secondary-market multifamily. Relevant for developers assessing upper-Midwest infill opportunities.

stories.title: Opus’ Kansas City Logistics Center Achieves Full Lease Up
stories.excerpt: Opus today announced that the Liberty Heartland Logistics Center in Liberty, Missouri, is fully stabilized. Liberty Heartland Logistics Center is a 1,659,570-square-foot three-building industrial park Opus developed and built on 165.57 acres, 20 miles outside of Kansas City, Missouri. Recent leasing activity at the development includes commitments from Wagner Logistics, a leading third-party logistics provider, for 317,000 square feet in Building B, which is located at 1401 Shepherd Road, as well as Dakota Bodies, a custom utility and service truck manufacturer, for 173,000 square feet in Building C, which is located at 1501 Shepherd Road. Liberty Heartland Logistics Center is a joint venture between Opus and Washington Capital Management, Inc. Michael VanBuskirk, Mark Long, John Hassler and Scott Bluhm of Newmark Zimmer marketed the buildings for lease. TAB USA began leasing 66,700 square feet at Liberty Heartland Logistics Center in 2024, followed by Animal Health International, which began leasing 255,000 square feet in 2025. Wagner Logistics and Dakota Bodies have since leased the remaining available space, bringing the development to full occupancy. The post Opus’ Kansas City Logistics Center Achieves Full Lease Up appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Opus' Liberty Heartland Logistics Center, Liberty, Mo., achieved full lease-up: 1.66M sf, 165 acres
Recent commitments: Wagner Logistics (317K sf), Dakota Bodies (173K sf); TAB USA, Animal Health Int'l prior
Kansas City industrial market absorbing large-format flex/logistics; proximity to I-74/80 corridors strong
stories.summary: Opus announced full stabilization of Liberty Heartland Logistics Center in Liberty, Missouri, a 1.66 million-square-foot, three-building industrial park on 165 acres, 20 miles from Kansas City. Recent leases include Wagner Logistics (317,000 sf) and Dakota Bodies (173,000 sf). Prior tenants include TAB USA (66,700 sf) and Animal Health International (255,000 sf). The project is a joint venture with Washington Capital Management.
stories.impact: No direct multifamily impact. Large-format industrial absorption and full lease-up signals strong logistics demand in Kansas City periphery, supporting broader employment and population in-migration that could drive future residential demand in suburban Kansas City markets.

stories.title: Manvel Investor Planning 1M-SF Retail Center, Medical Campus
stories.excerpt: Tharaldson Investors is pursuing an ambitious retail development in Manvel that is slated to include a 1 million-square-foot shopping center with retail and restaurant space and a 50-acre, $931 million MD Anderson Cancer Center campus. The proposed project is called Presidio Manvel. Tharaldson is partnering with United Commercial Development on the venture. The Houston Business Journal reports Tharaldson has secured Target and Kroger as anchors for the Manvel project, in addition to multiple food and beverage, fitness and other retail tenants. Steve Williamson with Transwestern is marketing the property. The cancer center plans to build its approximately 1 million-square-foot facility in two phases. The site is across Highway 288 from another large retail center under development, Weitzman’s 273-acre Manvel Town Center, which is anchored by H-E-B and Lowe’s. Tharaldson has developed a number of hotels in the market. The post Manvel Investor Planning 1M-SF Retail Center, Medical Campus appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Tharaldson Investors planning 1M-sf retail center + 50-acre MD Anderson Cancer Center, Manvel, Texas
Target and Kroger anchors secured; $931M cancer center in two phases; adjacent to Weitzman's Manvel Town Center
Major healthcare/retail mixed-use draw south of Houston; competition from nearby 273-acre Weitzman development
stories.summary: Tharaldson Investors, in partnership with United Commercial Development, is pursuing Presidio Manvel, a major mixed-use project including a 1 million-square-foot retail center anchored by Target and Kroger, plus a 50-acre, $931 million MD Anderson Cancer Center campus developed in two phases. The project is located across Highway 288 from Weitzman's 273-acre Manvel Town Center, anchored by H-E-B and Lowe's.
stories.impact: Manvel (south Houston exurb) is emerging as a significant employment and retail destination with dual major retail-anchored centers plus major medical campus. Multifamily developers should monitor this submarket for population and job-base growth tied to MD Anderson expansion; opportunity to acquire and build residential near major employment node, ahead of demand migration.

stories.title: Finmarc Management Completes Sale of Two-Building Industrial Property in Gaithersburg
stories.excerpt: Finmarc Management, Inc. has completed the $10.2 million disposition of 7419 Lindberg Drive, a two-building portfolio containing just under 46,000 square feet of industrial space, as well as 20,000 square feet of industrial outdoor storage land. The assets are located in the Gaithersburg section of Montgomery County, Maryland. KLNB’s Ken Fellows, Rob Pugh, and Lucas Glaeser represented Finmarc, and JLL’s Dan Coats represented the buyer, Rockville, Maryland-based National Technology Integrators. Aaron Rosenfeld of Kelley Drye & Warren LLP provided legal services to Finmarc. National Technology Integrators is a design-build contractor that plans to occupy the site, which consists of a 31,526-square-foot flex/warehouse building and a 14,483-square-foot storage building. The industrial building is equipped with 23-foot ceilings, three drive-in doors, and four loading docks. Delivered in 1986, both buildings were completely vacant at the time of the sale. The post Finmarc Management Completes Sale of Two-Building Industrial Property in Gaithersburg appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Finmarc Management sold 46K-sf industrial portfolio, Gaithersburg, Md., for $10.2M to National Technology Integrators
Two buildings (31.5K-sf flex/warehouse, 14.5K-sf storage); buyer plans owner-occupancy; vacant at sale
Gaithersburg industrial repositioning; tight Montgomery County supply supports value recovery
stories.summary: Finmarc Management completed the sale of a two-building industrial portfolio at 7419 Lindberg Drive in Gaithersburg, Maryland, for $10.2 million. The 46,000-square-foot property includes a 31,526-square-foot flex/warehouse building with 23-foot ceilings and a 14,483-square-foot storage building. Buyer National Technology Integrators plans owner-occupancy of the site, which was vacant at sale.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. Industrial asset sale to owner-occupant in Montgomery County suburbs. Relevant only as indicator of tight Gaithersburg/Baltimore industrial supply; tight logistics markets may signal population/employment growth in suburban Maryland, supporting peripheral multifamily demand in Montgomery/Howard County.
